cases.detail: Verilator 5.052 rejects a with range on a stream expression ("Unsupported: with[] stream expression" at {>>{up with [1 +: 2]}}, {>>{down with [4]}} and {>>{down with [4:2]}}, and at the dynamic array ranges i_data with [1 +: 3] in a pack and o_data with [0 +: o_len] in an unpack). IEEE 1800-2023 11.4.14.4 (Syntax 11-5) permits a with expression after any one-dimensional unpacked array and in a pack streams only the specified items, here up[1] and up[2], giving 32'h22330000, and the nonexistent-entry value of Table 7-1 (7.4.5) for an index outside byte down [3:0], so down with [4] gives 0 and down with [4:2] gives 32'h00112200; an unpack resizes a dynamic array to the range, which may read o_len unpacked before it. xezim 0.11.3 compiles the cases but ignores the ranges.

cases.detail: Verilator 5.052 generates C++ that g++ rejects for i = {>>{q, 16'h1234}} with an empty byte q[$] ("invalid cast from type 'VlQueue<unsigned char>' to type 'IData'"), and sizes the stream from the fixed operand alone (WIDTHEXPAND, 16 bits). IEEE 1800-2023 11.4.14.1 streams every element of a queue operand, none of an empty one, and 11.4.14 left-aligns the stream in the wider target, giving 32'h12340000. xezim 0.11.3 passes the case.

cases.detail: Verilator 5.052 generates C++ that g++ rejects for d = {<< byte {32'h11223344}} with byte d[]: it assigns the packed constant to the dynamic array ("no match for 'operator=' (operand types are 'VlQueue<unsigned char>' and 'unsigned int')"). IEEE 1800-2023 11.4.14 resizes a dynamically sized target to hold the stream, giving four elements 8'h44, 8'h33, 8'h22, 8'h11. Standalone probes also show Verilator right-aligning the stream of a queue in a wider fixed-size target, where 11.4.14 fills with zero bits on the right. xezim 0.11.3 compiles the case.

cases.detail: Verilator 5.052 unpacks {<< 3 {x, z}} = 8'b1101_0011 with logic [3:0] x, z into x = 4'b0110 and z = 4'b1011: it applies the re-ordering of the pack, 3-bit blocks sliced from the right with a 2-bit last block, to the source, so packing x and z again gives 8'b0111_0101. IEEE 1800-2023 11.4.14.3 makes the unpack the reverse operation of the pack of 11.4.14.2, giving x = 4'b1110 and z = 4'b0110, which pack back to the source; the two orders differ only when the last block is partial. xezim 0.11.3 gives the same values as Verilator.
